findings.issue_text: public/app/plugins/datasource/loki/querySplitting.ts:299 — applyTemplateVariables is now called once per query (via .map) instead of once per batch via interpolateVariablesInQueries; if the underlying implementation has any batch-level side effects (e.g. one-time variable "used" tracking, caching, or scopedVars mutation keyed to the whole request) these will now fire N times instead of once, which could double count usage analytics or repeat expensive work per query

goldens.comment: The applyTemplateVariables method is called with request.filters as the third parameter, but this parameter is not used in the corresponding test setup.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/plugins/datasource/loki/querySplitting.ts:299 — applyTemplateVariables is now called once per query (via .map) instead of once per batch via interpolateVariablesInQueries; if the underlying implementation has any batch-level side effects (e.g. one-time variable "used" tracking, caching, or scopedVars mutation keyed to the whole request) these will now fire N times instead of once, which could double count usage analytics or repeat expensive work per query

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a concrete behavioral change in how template interpolation is invoked: in `shardQuerySplitting.ts` it was previously a single batch call (`datasource.interpolateVariablesInQueries(request.targets, request.scopedVars)`) and is now done per-target via `.map((query) => datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters))`. This means any interpolation-related side effects or costs will now occur once per query rather than once per request. However, the finding’s specific reference to `querySplitting.ts` being changed from a prior batch interpolation call is not supported by the shown diff (that file previously did no interpolation at all).
